units.source: Keyboard Shortcuts
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts

units.source: This is supposed to be a complete list of keyboard shortcuts. Note that some of these may work only in certain contexts (e.g. in tree pane or note editor).
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts

units.source: Configuring keyboard shortcuts__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Configuring keyboard shortcuts

units.source: It is also possible to configure most keyboard shortcuts in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shortcuts__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Configuring keyboard shortcuts

units.source: On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Desktop Installation__TRILIUM_PH_1__, it's also possible to make shortcuts global by pressing on the globe icon near the key combination, which makes the shortcut work even without Trilium being in focus.
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Configuring keyboard shortcuts

units.source: Keyboard layouts__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Configuring keyboard shortcuts > Keyboard layouts

units.source: Shortcuts follow the characters printed on the keys of the active keyboard layout. On a French AZERTY keyboard, for example, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Z__TRILIUM_PH_3__ is the key labeled Z.
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Configuring keyboard shortcuts > Keyboard layouts

units.source: On a layout that doesn't type Latin letters, such as Russian, Greek or Hebrew, a key that types a letter of that alphabet counts as the key at the same position on a US QWERTY keyboard. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__J__TRILIUM_PH_3__ is then the key that types __TRILIUM_PH_4__ on a Russian keyboard, so shortcuts keep working without switching the layout first.
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Configuring keyboard shortcuts > Keyboard layouts

units.source: Keys that type punctuation still follow their own character. On a Russian keyboard, the key that types __TRILIUM_PH_0__ triggers __TRILIUM_PH_1__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_2__+__TRILIUM_PH_3__.__TRILIUM_PH_4__, not the shortcut of the US key at its position.
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Configuring keyboard shortcuts > Keyboard layouts

units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Note navigation

units.source: you can define a __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__ with e.g. value __TRILIUM_PH_3__ . Pressing this keyboard combination will then bring you to the note on which it is defined. Note that Trilium must be reloaded/restarted (__TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__R__TRILIUM_PH_7__ ) for changes to be in effect.
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Note navigation

units.source: See demo of some of these features in __TRILIUM_PH_0__note navigation__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

units.source: Context menus__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Context menus

units.source: Every context menu can be operated from the keyboard, however it was opened, for example with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ key in a text note to reach the spelling suggestions. These keys are fixed and cannot be changed in the options.
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Context menus

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__↑__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__↓__TRILIUM_PH_3__ – move to the previous / next item, skipping disabled ones and wrapping around at either end
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Context menus

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Home__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__End__TRILIUM_PH_3__ – move to the first / last item
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Context menus

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__→__TRILIUM_PH_1__ – open the submenu of the current item, or move to the next column in a submenu laid out in columns
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Context menus

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__←__TRILIUM_PH_1__ – move to the previous column, or close the submenu and go back to its item
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Context menus

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Space__TRILIUM_PH_3__ – run the current item, or open its submenu
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Context menus

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_1__ – close the innermost submenu, then the menu itself
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Context menus

units.source: typing the first letters of an item – jump to the next item whose title starts with them
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Context menus

units.source: With a right-to-left language, __TRILIUM_PH_0__←__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__→__TRILIUM_PH_3__ swap roles.
units.context: Keyboard Shortcuts > Shortcut reference > Context menus

units.source: Enter in tree pane switches from tree pane into note title. Enter from note title switches focus to text editor. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__.__TRILIUM_PH_3__ switches back from editor to tree pane.
